text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Trade Ministry issued decree on imports of 200,000 tonnes of barley exempt from customs duties until end-1996.
- Renel RA electricity authority bosses want to turn it into public utility to boost competition in electricity sector.
- Under government decision individual deposits of up to 10 million lei will be guaranteed and commercial banks will contribute 1.0 percent of their capital to creation of deposit insurance fund.
ADEVARUL
- Electricity consumption last month was 6,375 megawatts, 166 megawatts up on last August. Some 97 percent of consumption requirements were met from Renel's output.
- Manager of ARO SA carmaker said company -- whose exports were up and debts down -- was seeking association with foreign investor.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Rodae SA Romanian-South Korean carmaking venture manufactured 10,000 Cielo cars so far.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca said he accepted the offer of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) to run on its list for parliament in the November 3 polls.
- "Las Vegas of the Balkans" reads headline on one-page report on casinos in Bucharest, saying with its 18 casinos, the city is third in the world after Las Vegas and Monte Carlo.
- Report on international architecture contest held in Bucharest to reshape the area around the huge palace built by late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
ADEVARUL
- President Ion Iliescu will be the first on voting bulletins in the November 3 polls as he was the first to register his candidacy with the Central Electoral Bureau (BEC).
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Jail department asked for 20,000 convicts to be pardoned due to jail over-crowding.
- Schools not up to hygiene standards might be kept shut on September 15, when new school year starts, to prevent spread of meningitis epidemic.
- Academician Alexandru Balaban asked that Romania's English translation be changed from "Romania" into "Rumania" or "Roumania", alleging that the present form means "Gypsyhood".
ZIUA
- Newspaper picks up report from U.S. newspaper "San Diego Union Tribune" which said team of U.S. consultants were in Bucharest preparing Iliescu's campaign.

- Petre Roman, former reformist prime minister, head of opposition Democratic Party (PD) launches political programme for the presidential polls during convention of his Social Democratic Union (USD) alliance in which PD is major player.

- Human rights defence league (LADO) contested President Iliescu's candidacy stressing it was unconstitutional. LADO said it would take the case to The Hague Court of justice if local court accepts Iliescu's new presidential bid.
- Gyorgy Frunda, presidential candidate for the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) launches his campaign in the Transylvanian town of Tirgu Mures.
DIMINEATA
- "Ion Iliescu, Romania's President 1996-2000" reads banner headline of one-page report on official start of campaign for the November 3 presidential and parliamentary polls.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Alexandru Safran, former chief rabbi of Romania, living in Switzerland where he is since 1948 Geneva's chief rabbi, to attend launching ceremony of his book "La Cabala" in Romania.
VREMEA

- Adrian Paunescu, Socialist Labour Party (PSM) presidential candidate runs front-page report headlined "Irresponsible promises" on main promises made by Iliescu, ruling PDSR and opposition CDR during the campaign for the 1992 elections.
JURNALUL NATIONAL

- President Iliescu, dressed in denim shirt, gave 100,000 lei ($32) to an old woman in his first trip in the electoral campaign for the November 3 polls. ($=3,177 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
